summary: Hold: the hypothesis gates its own dispatch on the moe parent (1105a02aa3fa4e56) being faster than moe master at bs=1, and it was not (bs=1 50.93 us vs 48.37 us base, 0.975x), and the decode T=1 MoE chain it would replace is already cheaper than moe master's, so its case does not stand without the parent winning.
justification: Mechanism: replacing align + Marlin w13 + act_and_mul + Marlin w2 + post-norm combine at T=1 with one persistent kernel is plausible in principle (it saves 4-5 launches and the intermediate round trips). But the only measurement contradicts it. In muse_moe_w4a16, job 1105a02aa3fa4e56 did choose the fused path (bs=1 profile shows a single moe_bs1_kernel, 37.7 us), yet the scored bs=1 median was 50.93 us against 48.37 us for the moe base (triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack): 0.975x, flat-to-slower, with the outcome neutral within CI. The 37.7 us profiled kernel time against the base's ~51 us kernel sum (Marlin 44.6 + combine 3.4 + act 1.6 + align 1.6) did not turn into a wall-clock win under graph replay, so the persistent kernel's real cost (flag reset, spin-up, all-CTA co-residency, whatever the profile does not capture) eats the fusion saving. Decode makes this worse, not better. Decode's T=1 Marlin is already 40.2 us (FINDINGS, decode_1 sliding and full) against moe master's 44.6, and decode times every replay with a cold L2 (TASK.md). So the incumbent chain the fused kernel must beat is about 4 us cheaper than the one it already failed to beat. The expected '-20..-30 us, +15-20%' assumes the fused kernel takes its own target (~20 us); the measured 37.7 us kernel / ~47 us wall leaves no visible gain. Weakest link: the expected magnitude rests on the moe target time, not the measured moe result. The hypothesis's own Risk section says to hold unless bs=1 was faster than moe master, which it was not.
confounders: small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl (base, rewrite stage 1): the T<=32 dense chain runs PDL-launched kernels (cudaLaunchKernelEx with programmatic serialization) around the MoE. A persistent kernel that spins on device flags and assumes all 132 CTAs are co-resident could see its CTAs scheduled late, or contend with a PDL-early-launched neighbour. That would change its time, or hang it, in a way the moe harness never exercised.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-t: replaced the T=1 post-expert combine with a Triton kernel. The fused kernel also takes over this step, so any decode_1 delta mixes the fusion with removing an already-optimised combine. The saving available from this step is smaller than in the moe base it was compared against.
marlin-block-m-cap-16: block_m stays 8 at T=1, so it does not change the incumbent the fused kernel replaces at T=1. No real confounding.
interference: No companions. A companion only helps when a single result would be ambiguous. Here the decision is upstream: the parent's measured bs=1 result already says the fused kernel does not beat a Marlin chain that is slower than decode's, and the hypothesis's own condition for dispatch is unmet. A revert of small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl (the PDL chain) would be the only sensible ab-revert, to test persistent-kernel and PDL interaction, but spending a check on that before the fused kernel is shown to win standalone is not justified. The right next step is a moe-side stage-2 rewrite (cuda-fused-moe-bs1-persistent-w13-silu-w2 follow-up) that shows bs=1 below moe master's 48.4 us. Re-mint the port after that.
rules_flags: Persistent kernel with a device-flag grid barrier: the flags must be reset on device inside the captured graph (a memset node or an in-kernel epilogue reset), never from the host. Otherwise replays after the first deadlock or read stale flags.

The co-residency assumption (all 132 CTAs resident) is not guaranteed inside the decode graph when PDL is enabled on neighbouring kernels. This is a hang risk in the timed call, not a rules breach, but a hang fails the run.

The 16-byte pointer check in _fused_forward is host-side branching on tensor addresses. It is decided once at capture, which is fine for graph replay, but it must not fall back to a different path between capture and replay. Confirm the fallback is decided in prepare() or at capture only.
_fused_setup's self-check and repack run in prepare() on weights, not on per-call data. That is allowed, provided nothing derived from data is cached.
open_questions: Why did the moe fused kernel's 37.7 us profiled time become a 50.9 us scored median, worse than the base's 48.4 us? If the cause is fixable (flag reset or spin-up overhead, a cold-L2 effect), the fix belongs in a moe stage-2 rewrite before any port.
Does the decode graph's PDL chain ever early-launch the kernel after the experts, so that it occupies SMs while the persistent kernel's CTAs are still unscheduled?
Would the port compete with or supersede moe-small-t-cuda-swapab-port at T=1? That parent failed its tests, so neither T=1 MoE port currently has a winning parent.
